company.name: sweetgreen
company.oneLiner: sweetgreen runs restaurants serving salads, warm bowls, and plates, with ordering through its app, office batch delivery, and catering.
company.customers: Individual diners ordering in store, in the app, and online; office teams through Outpost; and groups from 10 to 10,000+ people through catering.

blueprint.headline: sweetgreen's Outpost and catering orders arrive with a cutoff or 24 hours of notice, so the agents to build first turn that known demand into prep, dispatch, and quotes before the lunch rush.

agents.name: Outpost Batch Planner
agents.role: Forecasts each office's daily Outpost batch and turns it into prep and dispatch plans for the restaurant that serves it.
agents.trigger: Daily, 90 minutes before each office's Outpost cutoff, then again at cutoff
does: Projects the batch size for each Outpost office from orders so far and that office's history
Adds the projected batch to the serving restaurant's prep plan by menu item
Groups offices into drop routes that meet each agreed delivery time

humanGate.detail: Prep adjustments apply automatically within 15 percent of the usual batch. Larger changes, and any change to an office's delivery time, need the general manager.

agents.evidence: Outpost is described as a daily batch delivery to the office with a cutoff set per office, and orders arrive through the app or online ordering.
agents.impact: Outpost batches are prepped from a forecast instead of a last-minute scramble at cutoff, and drops arrive at the agreed time.

agents.name: Catering Quote Desk
agents.role: Turns catering inquiries into complete, priced quotes that follow the published catering rules.
agents.trigger: When a Start Catering Inquiry form or catering email arrives
does: Extracts headcount, date, address, and format: individually packaged or the Sweetgreen Bar
Checks the $50 minimum, the 24-hour notice rule, the 20-mile delivery radius, and whether the Sweetgreen Bar is offered at that location
Drafts a quote with the 10 percent delivery fee (minimum $30) and the nearest catering location

humanGate.detail: A catering coordinator approves every quote before it is sent. Orders over 500 people, or inside 24 hours, go to the catering manager.

agents.evidence: The catering page sets a $50 minimum, 24 hours notice, delivery within 20 miles at a 10 percent fee starting at $30, and offers the Sweetgreen Bar only at select locations.
agents.impact: Inquiries get an accurate quote quickly, and coordinators review instead of looking up radius, minimums, and location menus by hand.

agents.name: Allergen Guide Checker
agents.role: Checks that the Nutrition and Allergens Guide matches the current recipes before a menu change goes live at any location.
agents.trigger: When a recipe or seasonal menu change is scheduled
does: Compares each changed recipe's ingredients against the published allergen and nutrition entries
Lists every location whose menu includes the changed item
Blocks the change in the menu system until the guide is updated or a reviewer clears it

humanGate.detail: Only the food safety lead can release a held menu change. The agent can hold a change; it can never publish one.

agents.evidence: The site publishes a Nutrition and Allergens Guide while menus vary by location and feature changing items such as the Harvest Bowl and Miso Glazed Salmon.
agents.impact: Allergen information stays correct as recipes change across locations, which protects diners first and the brand second.

agents.name: New Location Demand Digest
agents.role: Combines location requests and Outpost interest into a monthly demand map for the real estate team.
agents.trigger: First business day of each month
does: Reads submissions to the Where should we open next form and new Outpost sign-up requests
Clusters them by neighborhood and office building, counting distinct companies and requests
Writes a ranked internal digest with the strongest unserved areas

humanGate.detail: It reads form submissions and writes an internal report. It contacts no one and commits to nothing.

agents.evidence: The Locations page asks visitors where sweetgreen should open next, and Outpost has its own sign-up for offices that want the program.
agents.impact: Site selection gets a steady signal of where people already want sweetgreen, named down to the office building.

firstBuild.why: Every quote is already reviewed by a coordinator, the rules are written down on the catering page, and each faster quote is revenue.
scope: Read inquiries from the catering form and inbox
Check minimum, notice, radius, and Sweetgreen Bar availability by location
Draft priced quotes for coordinator approval
Track approval edits to find which rules the drafts get wrong

blueprint.nonObvious: Outpost is the one sweetgreen channel where demand is committed before prep: orders close at a per-office cutoff and go out in one batch. That makes Outpost history the cleanest training data in the company, and a forecast calibrated on it can then correct prep for walk-in and app orders at the same restaurant.
caveats: Curated by hand from the public site, not produced by a live run.
The catering page states both a 24-hour and a 12-hour notice window; the quote desk assumes 24 hours until the catering team confirms.
Kitchen, dispatch, and recipe systems are not visible on the site and are named by category.
